name: ecommerce-customer-accounts
description: The person's standing to act: claims, saved lists, and the privacy request as a case with participants.
features: A privacy request is a case with a lawful basis, a deadline in a named timezone and one row per participant
The participant registry is explicit configuration; an unregistered module is invisible and that is a defect, not a default
A request whose participants did not all answer is concluded as partial, naming who did not answer, never as done
Request scope is a first-class field because the fleet disagrees: one merchant or the person everywhere
A participant that answered at a different scope than the request asked for is recorded as a mismatch
One consumed contract for every participating module; no sibling module is depended on or called directly
Nothing is erased inside an HTTP request: participants are commissioned as separate retryable steps
An export is assembled from recorded contributions and is delivered as partial when one is missing
A guest order claim is proof-of-possession: reference plus email, completed by a token, never a lookup
A wrong order reference and a wrong email are indistinguishable, so the claim path is not an order oracle
Failed claim attempts are recorded and rate-limited, because the failures are the security signal
Saved lists hold product references and quantities, never a price, and never a priced cart line
A share is its own revocable aggregate belonging to the list, not a single token on the person
Concluding an erasure revokes every share the subject holds and clears this module's own rows
No password, no token and no second factor is read or written; re-authentication is recorded, never held
